problem: Learning complex, subjective safety constraints from human feedback in reinforcement learning is data-inefficient because humans can only provide limited expert demonstrations.
approach: PbCRL uses preference learning with a novel dead-zone mechanism to capture heavy-tailed safety cost distributions, combined with SNR loss for exploration and two-stage training to reduce online labeling burden.
contribution: Achieves superior alignment with true safety requirements and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on safety and reward metrics.

problem: Large language models lack efficient post-training methods to improve reasoning abilities without extensive supervised data.
approach: One-shot Entropy Minimization applies entropy minimization over a single unlabeled example with ~10 gradient steps, inducing a right-skewed logit shift that amplifies high-probability tokens.
contribution: Substantially improves reasoning across mathematical, logical, and coding domains as a fully unsupervised post-training approach.

problem: LLMs exhibit belief drift in multiple-choice question answering, violating the martingale property required for coherent Bayesian inference.
approach: Prompted Predictive Resampling (PPR) generates repeated answers to the same question to expose belief drift; uses seed-answer prompting and self-consistency fine-tuning loss to accelerate stabilization.
contribution: Substantially reduces belief drift and improves predictive coherence on multiple-choice QA benchmarks without sacrificing accuracy.

problem: Large language models perform arithmetic poorly, indicating a disconnect between internal neural representations and discrete outputs.
approach: Identifies Iso-Raw-Sum Trajectory (IRST) manifold geometry and proposes Noisy Quantization Model framing arithmetic errors as topological slippages of continuous carry potential across quantization thresholds.
contribution: Provides geometric framework explaining arithmetic failures and enables geometric consistency checks that detect and correct quantization errors during inference.

problem: LLM backdoor attacks fail to persist when users perform supervised fine-tuning because poisoning creates a narrow, sharp basin vulnerable to parameter drift.
approach: BAD-BOOM uses broader smoothness minimization with Fisher-induced ellipsoidal constraint to allocate larger perturbation budgets to backdoor-sensitive parameters, widening the backdoor basin.
contribution: Consistently preserves high attack success rate across multiple LLMs and SFT scenarios while maintaining competitive utility.

problem: Softmax attention diffuses probability mass to irrelevant tokens at long sequence lengths, and lowering temperature to sharpen focus causes vanishing gradients.
approach: LUCID Attention applies a preconditioner derived from exponentiated key-key similarities that minimizes key overlap in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space, enabling focused retrieval without temperature lowering.
contribution: Achieves up to 18% improvement on BABILong and 14% on RULER long-context retrieval tasks with same computational complexity as standard attention.

problem: Vision-Language Model prompt learning neglects spectral (frequency) granularity of visual signals, focusing only on text optimization while treating visual encoders as frozen holistic extractors.
approach: SpecPL decomposes visual signals via VAE into semantic low-frequency bands and granular high-frequency details; uses counterfactual granule training by permuting high-frequency signals to enforce visual-semantic distinction.
contribution: Achieves 81.51% harmonic-mean accuracy as a universal plug-and-play booster for text-oriented baselines on 11 benchmarks.

problem: Adapting frozen MLLMs for dense retrieval while preserving pre-trained semantic space is challenging because invasive parameter updates may impair reasoning capability.
approach: SLQ uses Shared Latent Queries appended to both text and image tokens, leveraging native causal attention to aggregate multimodal context into unified embedding; constructs KARR-Bench for knowledge-aware reasoning retrieval.
contribution: Outperforms full fine-tuning and LoRA on COCO and Flickr30K while achieving substantial gains on knowledge-aware retrieval.

problem: Existing multilingual policy optimization restricts each training question to a single response language or uses fixed dominant-language supervision, limiting diversity of training signals.
approach: Language-Routed Policy Optimization (LRPO) treats language as selectable variable, eliciting multilingual rollouts and using multi-armed bandit language router to adaptively balance exploration-exploitation of language quality.
contribution: Consistently improves multilingual performance by enabling adaptive language routing for cross-lingual knowledge exploitation.

problem: While frozen self-supervised representations transfer well with few labels within tasks, understanding why they generalize across many tasks without interference remains unclear.
approach: Shows that directional CDNV (decision-axis variance) controls both few-shot transfer and multitask interference; proves sharp non-asymptotic generalization bounds and links decision-axis collapse to orthogonal task geometry.
contribution: Provides geometric explanation for few-shot transfer in self-supervised learning with bounds that track practical few-shot error.

problem: Existing exam-style benchmarks focus on understanding and reasoning rather than rigorous drawing tasks, lacking precise evaluation of semantic correctness and visual plausibility in image generation.
approach: GenExam introduces 1,000 samples across 10 subjects with four-level taxonomy, each with ground-truth images and fine-grained scoring points evaluating semantic correctness and visual plausibility.
contribution: Reveals large gap between open-source and closed-source models, providing rigorous assessment of integrated understanding, reasoning, and generation.

problem: LLMs excel at one-on-one instruction but struggle with one-to-many alignment (e.g., clinical ward rounds) due to context dilution and goal misalignment across diverse trainees.
approach: ClinTutor-R1 is a multimodal agent with explicit internal thinking mechanism modeling individual belief states and group consensus, trained via multi-agent pedagogical simulator (ClinEdu) and large-scale Socratic dialogue dataset (ClinTeach).
contribution: Outperforms base models by over 20% and achieves parity with reasoning models while maintaining scalability across expanding cohorts.

problem: Data-free compression methods like NF4 suffer functional collapse below 4 bits, while data-dependent methods require calibration data and extensive training.
approach: EntQuant decouples numerical precision from storage cost via entropy coding, compressing a 70B model in under 10 minutes using only quantization without recovery training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and instruction-tuned models while retaining functional performance at modest inference overhead.

problem: Diffusion models produce highly curved trajectories and noisy score targets due to memoryless forward process with independent data-noise coupling.
approach: Adjoint Schrödinger Bridge Matching (ASBM) recovers optimal trajectories by viewing SB forward dynamic as coupling construction and learning backward generative dynamic with matching loss supervised by induced optimal coupling.
contribution: Produces significantly straighter and more efficient sampling paths with improved stability, scaling to high-dimensional image generation with fewer steps.

problem: Large language models reveal and amplify societal biases during chain-of-thought generation, yet existing mitigation methods require retraining or auxiliary systems.
approach: COFT applies training-free token-level fairness control at decode time: creates masked counterfactual prompt, applies logit fusion to attenuate attribute-driven biases, and uses conformal calibration for candidate token set certification.
contribution: Reduces bias metrics by 30-55% (median 38%) while preserving task utility, language quality, and reasoning accuracy with <11% computational overhead.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models exhibit large discontinuities in accuracy-compute trade-offs because once selected, experts execute fully without width variation.
approach: MoSE introduces nested, slimmable expert structure enabling variable-width execution; combines multi-width training with standard MoE objectives and uses lightweight test-time training to map router confidence to expert widths.
contribution: Matches or improves standard MoE at full width and shifts compute-quality frontier toward lower inference FLOPs with continuous accuracy-compute spectrum.

problem: Subgoal-based policy tree search requires explicit subgoal generation incurring substantial overhead, limiting scalability to complex environments.
approach: Uses learned rerooter through √LTS algorithm that implicitly decomposes problems into soft subtasks; proposes three rerooter designs: clustering-based (exploiting global structure), heuristic-based (leveraging cost-to-go), and hybrid.
contribution: Scales to complex environments where explicit subgoal methods fail while achieving state-of-the-art online training efficiency.

problem: As LLMs act as autonomous agents with tool access in sandboxed environments, evaluating their capacity to escape these sandboxes is critical for security assurance.
approach: SandboxEscapeBench is a CTF-style benchmark with nested sandbox architecture covering misconfiguration, privilege errors, kernel flaws, and runtime/orchestration weaknesses.
contribution: Shows LLMs can identify and exploit sandbox vulnerabilities when present, demonstrating need for rigorous evaluation to ensure sandboxing remains effective.

problem: Large multimodal models lack explicit taxonomic knowledge, leading to poor hierarchical visual recognition consistency despite strong general capabilities.
approach: HiR² introduces hierarchical representation regularization combining taxonomic entailment loss (via hyperbolic cones) and discriminative dispersive loss (angular separation on unit sphere) for semantic-aware visual tree extraction.
contribution: Effectively captures taxonomic structures across diverse LMMs and fine-tuning methods, improving hierarchical consistency.

problem: Graph generative models struggle to scale to large, complex structures while maintaining node and edge feature generation for real-world applications.
approach: FAHNES is a hierarchical framework generating topology and features jointly via node coarsening and localized expansion, guided by hierarchical scale encoding for cross-scale consistency.
contribution: Achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance while uniquely scaling to featured large-scale graphs and hypergraphs.

problem: Value factorization in MARL relies on static coordination assumptions that hinder generalization on long-horizon tasks with shifting inter-agent dependencies.
approach: TACTIC combines VQ-VAE trajectory abstraction for discrete task classes, semantic-conditioned sparse coordination graphs that prune edges by variance-based payoff sensitivity, and frozen trajectory-class predictor.
contribution: Shows strong competitiveness with adaptive coordination under sparse rewards and dynamic task structures on SMAC and SUMO.

problem: Existing lipid-binding protein predictors use fully supervised training treating unlabeled samples as negatives, creating systematic false negatives due to missing evidence.
approach: LipoPU formulates lipid-binding learning as ranking-based positive-unlabeled objective at pocket level, using attention-based representations robust to ambiguous pocket definitions.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains over supervised baselines and identifies biologically informative residues via structural case studies.

problem: Traditional image forgery localization methods depend on physical noise absent in synthetic data, failing against realistic AI-generated forgeries.
approach: FLAME theoretically demonstrates diffusion inherently suppresses local high-frequency variance creating energy gaps; uses LAD map to capture anomalies with parameter-efficient SAM adapter; introduces EditStream for continuous synthetic data generation.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art results on AI-generated forgery datasets while generalizing to unseen generative architectures.

problem: Constrained optimization algorithms struggle with difficult-to-project constraints and lack adaptive step-size schemes for parameter-free performance.
approach: Uses randomized feasibility algorithm with Polyak steps and adaptive sampling of constraints per iteration; decouples constraint satisfaction from objective minimization.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence in expectation for strongly convex objectives and O(1/√T) rate for nonsmooth objectives with problem parameter-free adaptive stepsizes.

problem: Obtaining simultaneous confidence bounds for aggregated effects over data-selected subsets requires computationally intractable nonlinear combinatorial optimization.
approach: Casts weighted densest-subgraph problem as exact linear and mixed integer linear programs; develops fully polynomial-time approximation scheme exploiting rank-1 structure.
contribution: Establishes finite-sample coverage guarantee with lighter subset-family dependence than classical methods and demonstrates scalability on synthetic and ML applications.

problem: Code generation models hallucinate, producing functionally incorrect code that hinders deployment in safety-critical systems due to difficulty identifying correctness without test suites.
approach: Automatically generates unit tests via dynamic code analysis; proposes selective generator that abstains from uncertain generations based on functional correctness; uses generated tests in both learning and evaluation.
contribution: Theoretically controls false discovery rate among non-abstained answers while enabling precise code evaluation and functional correctness verification.

problem: DNA language models depend critically on tokenization strategy, yet fixed tokenizations are brittle under shifts, indels, and local repeats because DNA lacks canonical boundaries.
approach: DNAChunker introduces learnable adaptive segmentation module producing context-dependent, variable-length units; learns to allocate finer granularity to enriched regions while compressing repetitive sequences.
contribution: Consistently improves over fixed-tokenization baselines on five benchmarks with learned segmentation that is mutation-resilient and biologically-informed.

problem: Existing representational similarity metrics lack rigorous theoretical grounding linking functional and representational similarity across dimensions.
approach: Unifies three dimensions through usable information framework: establishes formal link between stitching and conditional mutual information; reveals similarity is relative to predictive family capacity; shows representational similarity is sufficient but not necessary for functional similarity.
contribution: Provides unified theoretical and empirical synthesis linking functional, representational similarity and reconstruction via task-granularity hierarchy.

problem: Open-vocabulary object detection approaches distill regional features for semantic alignment but sacrifice spatial fidelity when using distilled features for both classification and localization.
approach: OSSD explicitly decouples semantic and spatial learning: distills object semantics from CLIP global embeddings for region discrimination and injects spatial priors from base-trained detector; proposes Location Quality Estimation Head.
contribution: Achieves 49.2 AP50 on OV-COCO (3.6% above previous best) and 40.5 mAP on novel categories in OV-LVIS.

problem: Modern AI hardware adopts low-precision floating-point formats for LLMs, yet unified comparison of FP versus INT quantization across granularities has been missing.
approach: Systematically investigates FP-INT trade-offs revealing critical performance crossover: FP excels in coarse-grained quantization, INT surpasses in fine-grained; introduces symmetric clipping resolving gradient bias in fine-grained INT training.
contribution: Demonstrates MXINT8 and MXINT4 superior to FP counterparts in accuracy and hardware efficiency, challenging current hardware trajectories.

problem: Open-vocabulary segmentation produces blurred boundaries and fragmented structures because image-level training in CLIP mixes amplitude and phase information limiting fine-grained discrimination.
approach: PhaseAlign decouples magnitude and phase of visual-textual embeddings in complex domain; introduces spatial-aware cross-modal projection modeling local relations via multi-scale contrast, and attention-guided affinity propagating activations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks with improved boundary clarity and region integrity.

problem: Rigid integer-based bit-widths in quantization create deployment gap where LLMs cannot fit optimally to specific memory budgets.
approach: LiftQuant enables continuous bit-width control via lift-then-project mechanism: approximates low-dimensional vectors by projecting 1-bit lattice from higher-dimensional lifted space; effective bit-width is ratio of lifted to original dimension.
contribution: Enables 70B LLM compression to 2.4 bits for 24GB GPU with performance significantly surpassing standard 2-bit models.

problem: Masked diffusion model samplers remain greedy, selecting locally certain tokens without accounting for downstream effects, increasing cumulative uncertainty.
approach: Info-Gain Sampler uses MDM bidirectional structure to balance immediate uncertainty with information gained over remaining positions; training-free decoding method.
contribution: Improves average reasoning accuracy by 2.9-11.6 points and achieves 62.8% win rate in creative writing across reasoning, coding, and generation tasks.

problem: Diffusion models suffer high inference latency while flow-based policy methods require complex constraints; applying MeanFlow to robotics faces spectral bias and gradient starvation in low-velocity regimes.
approach: One-step MeanFlow Policy (OMP) introduces lightweight directional alignment synchronizing predicted velocities with true mean velocities; implements Differential Derivation Equation to approximate Jacobian-Vector Product.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on Adroit and Meta-World with superior success rate and trajectory accuracy while maintaining single-step efficiency.

problem: Existing 3D scene generation methods prioritize visual plausibility but neglect protocol grounding and safety constraints essential for scientific experimentation in automated laboratories.
approach: LabBuilder operates through three tightly coupled components: LabForge curates meta-dataset and translates specifications into protocols; LabGen synthesizes layouts via constraint-aware optimization; LabTouchstone evaluates layouts as benchmark.
contribution: Generates realistic laboratory environments valid under geometric, chemical-safety, and navigation constraints with significantly improved performance.

problem: Gradient testing and estimation rely on expensive function evaluations, but learning using only comparison oracle is understudied.
approach: Designs gradient testing algorithm using O(1) queries to determine if normalized gradient is ε-close or 2ε-far from target; gradient estimation using O(n log(1/ε)) queries proven optimal.
contribution: Establishes optimal query complexity for gradient estimation and develops quantum algorithm achieving O(log(n/ε)) queries.

problem: Federated continual learning of LLMs faces communication-stability-plasticity trilemma; naively uploading all layers increases forgetting despite improved plasticity.
approach: RieSelect treats stability as staying within Fisher-metric safe basin; derives layer-wise conflict score and certified safe step size; formulates selective uplink as knapsack-based utility-risk selection.
contribution: Improves average accuracy by 18.99-28.14 points while reducing total uplink by 53-115× under standard communication protocols.

problem: Sampling from non-log-concave distributions with difference-of-convex regularizers combines smooth data fidelity and non-smooth DC structure.
approach: DC-LA applies Moreau envelopes to DC components separately and studies proximal Langevin algorithm with DC structure exploitation.
contribution: Establishes convergence to target distribution in q-Wasserstein distance for all q, improving prior work with more general framework and assumptions.

problem: Conditional sampling from partially observed distributions requires additional feature information but contemporary methods lack efficient one-shot inference.
approach: CGMMD frames conditional sampling as direct adversary-free minimization; uses nearest-neighbor kernels enabling single-pass generation; establishes convergence bounds and concentration results.
contribution: Performs competitively on synthetic complex densities and practical applications like image denoising and super-resolution with low test-time complexity.

problem: Autoregressive PDE surrogates violate global conservation and physical bounds over long rollouts, destabilizing predictions for conservation laws.
approach: FluxNet learns cumulative transport amounts via capacity-constrained transport heads (L/U/D) enforcing lower/upper/dual bounds; no temporal integration required enabling large-timestep prediction.
contribution: Achieves exact conservation, structural bound preservation, modularity, and superior stability at large temporal strides on 1D/2D benchmarks.
